reason: Strassen ranks first because it is approved and is the only proposal that reduces the main 512-square multiply work. Its 12.5% MAC reduction is arithmetic evidence only; timed copying and recombination plus FP32 accuracy risk make validation essential. The cache_blocking and n512_fast_path proposals substantially duplicate its three-buffer schedule, so treat them as overlapping advice rather than independent gains. Panel packing tests a distinct, bounded workspace change on the timed path. Transpose fusion may remove scratch traffic, but repeats conversion across output blocks. The remaining proposals have weaker relevance to the fixed n=512 goal: general-size tail handling and the C fallback do not change that path; tile mapping and FMOPA order have limited evidence of benefit. The assembly proposal depends on an unverified legal post-index form and should be checked before implementation.
